references.text: Jacob erects a stone pillar and pours oil over it at the place where God revealed himself to him in a dream – the first event in Bethel that 35:14 looks back on.
Jacob vows that the stone he has erected will become a house of God, which he now fulfills by returning to Bethel.
Jacob erects a stone pillar as a witness to the covenant between him and Laban – part of Jacob's pattern of raising stone pillars on important occasions.
God commands Jacob to go to Bethel and build an altar there – the direct background for why Jacob raises the stone pillar at this place.
Moses erects twelve stone pillars at Mount Sinai as a covenant witness – a parallel to Jacob's use of stone pillars as memorials of God's revelation.
Instructions about drink offerings (nesek) that are to be poured out before the Lord – the same practice that Jacob performs over the stone pillar in Bethel.
Describes the content of the vow that Jacob made at the same divine revelation where he erected the stone.
Both use an erected stone as a permanent witness that God has spoken and given words.
